cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Anything but That Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every attempt to discuss the one detail that could expose your real motive or involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give you the spare key over dinner. Have you booked a table?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I never gave you a spare. Where did it come from?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One arrangement at a time, please. We need a confirmed table before we discuss what happens over it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's confirmed for two. Did my sister give you the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we're including your sister, we need three places. Ring the restaurant before you invite anyone else.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 treats B2's key-source question as a sequencing mistake; A5 uses B4's sister mention and confirmed count to supervise a new dinner task, keeping the exposing question unanswered.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks where the unoffered key came from. A3 evades through booking sequence; B4 closes that task and names a possible source, so A5 converts sister involvement into guest-count work.

relationship.evidence: B2 has a legitimate access concern and B4 both answers logistics and pursues the source. A's distraction does not require B to abandon that concern willingly.

heightening.evidence: A5 exploits B4's attempt to close the dinner topic to open a more specific reservation correction, sustaining the same evasive behavior.

specificity.evidence: A1 key return over dinner, B2 no gift and B4 booking for two identify the undisclosed fact and available distraction.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's instruction to ring the restaurant is the action A wants instead of an origin inquiry; it is not an explanation of evasion to the reader.

coach2.stated: A1 has spare key; B2 never gave it; B4 has dinner booked for two and asks whether sister supplied it.
coach2.inferred: A opportunistically treats mentioning the sister as including her in dinner; this is purposeful evasion, not a fact the report endorses.
coach2.missing: The actual key source remains the detail A refuses to discuss.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate: the false guest-count premise is visibly A's distraction and is conditional rather than a silently established invitation.
